sections.h2: Where Bluffton sits and why it matters
sections.html:
Bluffton is a town in southern Beaufort County, mostly along US 278 between Hilton Head Island and Interstate 95. Jasper County shares the metropolitan area but does not contain the town. The 2020 count was 27,716 residents, and the estimate for 2025 is 36,807.

The layout has a quirk for sellers. Strict state annexation laws left unincorporated pockets, called doughnut holes, inside the town limits. So a Bluffton mailing address doesn't guarantee town rules. The lot may fall under the county instead, which changes the answer on permits and rental licenses.

sections.h2: Growth, associations and what buyers ask
sections.html:
Bluffton's population grew 882.7 percent from 2000 to 2010 and another 121.2 percent from 2010 to 2020. Planned developments from the early housing boom drove much of it, and several stayed partly unfinished after the Great Recession. A house here can sit in a community with a homeowners association, a master plan or amenities still under development.

  • Request the association's governing documents and any unpaid dues ahead of a contract.
  • Find out if your lot is in town limits or in a doughnut hole.
  • Collect any plat, survey and permit records you have, since the county's recording rules ask for a legal description or a reference to a recorded plat.

Bluffton is in South Carolina's Southern Coastal Hurricane Region, and Beaufort County has a single evacuation zone, so an order applies to the whole county. The Bluffton Township Fire District, (843) 757-2800, points residents to the state's zone maps at Hurricane.SC and a town evacuation routes PDF.

The yearly rainfall is about 50.4 inches, and the elevation is only about 20 feet. Buyers in a coastal county reasonably ask about wind and water, so gather the roof age, past claims and any flood paperwork you have.

Town Ordinance 2023-248 regulates short-term rentals, which it defines as renting a residential dwelling for fewer than 30 days. If the house is used that way, the rules can affect a sale.

  • Operating a short-term rental takes a Town Clerk license unless an exemption is granted.
  • Licenses last a calendar year and are posted visibly at the property.
  • The clerk can suspend, revoke or decline to renew a license for good cause.
  • An affected person can appeal to the Town Manager within 10 days of written notice, then to Town Council within another 10. Council has the last word.

Anyone buying a rental will want to know if the license is current and whether the home is inside the town.

sections.h2: Property tax for a Bluffton seller
sections.html:
Beaufort County reassessed in 2023, and the next reassessment is set for 2028. State law requires one every five years.

Owners who apply get 4 percent of appraised value on a primary residence, while other residential and commercial property sits at 6 percent. Applications for the 4 percent rate are open from January 1 to January 15 of the following year. That window also covers an objection to value, as does a 90-day period after an assessment notice, though one tax year allows only one of the two.

Selling counts as an assessable transfer of interest, with a December 31 appraisal date in the transfer year and the new value taking effect the following tax year. A county transfer exemption can trim market value by as much as 25 percent without dropping below the current record, and its application is due ahead of January 31. Questions go to the Assessor, (843) 255-2400.

The bill can be paid through January 15. After that the state adds 3 percent on January 16, 7 percent more following the second of February and 5 percent more after March 17.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Beaufort County
sections.html:
Take deeds to 100 Ribaut Road in Beaufort, where the Beaufort County Register of Deeds keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Call (843) 255-2555.

The county's checklist is long. Expect a return-to name and address, two witnesses who aren't parties to the deal, a notary block, a legal description, the grantee's address, a district, map and parcel number and a derivation clause. Warranty deeds add a preparation clause.

Fees are a flat $15 for the deed plus the combined state and county charge of $1.85 per $500 of price. An extra transfer fee on Hilton Head Island applies only to certain district numbers. Three e-recording companies are accepted, and anything arriving after 4:30 p.m. is processed the next business day.

An attorney must supervise a South Carolina closing, and that attorney can confirm current fees.

sections.h2: Getting ready for a fast sale in Bluffton
sections.html:
Begin with three questions. Which government covers the lot? Does an association have a say? Has the house been a rental? Those answers show which permits, dues and licenses a buyer will ask about.

Then build the file: deed, plat and survey, flood papers, roof age, past insurance claims, association documents and a rental license if you have one. A complete file speeds up every step that follows.

Finally, choose between a listing and a cash sale. Cash buyers purchase the house as it is, which blunts the effect of an aging roof or an unclear permit question. A closing attorney still handles the closing and recording.

A seller in a coastal county should expect questions about water. Pull together any flood elevation or zone paperwork, the current insurance declarations and a list of claims, with dates and what was repaired. Buyers' lenders ask for these, and a prepared seller avoids last-minute delays.

Know the evacuation facts too. The county's single zone means an evacuation order covers every address, so a closing scheduled during hurricane season can be pushed back. Build some slack into the calendar and keep the attorney informed.

sections.h2: Working with the town and the county
sections.html:
Ask the attorney to walk through the deed checklist with you well ahead of the closing. Missing witnesses, a notary block left blank or a legal description that differs from the plat are the kinds of defects that hold up recording, and fixing them costs days. Gather the grantee's address and the district, map and parcel number early, since the county asks for all of them.

Questions about permits and rental licenses go to the Town of Bluffton at 843-706-4500 if the lot is inside the limits. Questions about value, exemptions and the 4 percent application go to the county Assessor. Deed and plat questions go to the Register of Deeds. Keeping each question with the right office saves calls.

faqs.q: Is Bluffton, SC in Beaufort County or Jasper County?
faqs.a: Beaufort County. Jasper County is part of the same metropolitan area but does not contain the town.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Bluffton house short term?
faqs.a: Yes, a Town Clerk license is required under Town Ordinance 2023-248 for stays under 30 days unless an exemption applies. It lasts one calendar year.

faqs.q: When is Beaufort County's next reassessment?
faqs.a: 2028, after the last one in 2023. State law requires one every five years.

faqs.q: Will a sale raise the property tax on a Bluffton house?
faqs.a: It can. Reappraisal follows a sale, dated December 31 of that year and effective the next tax year, though a transfer exemption may cut the value by up to 25 percent.

faqs.q: Does Beaufort County evacuate by zone?
faqs.a: No. There is a single evacuation zone, so an order covers the whole county.
